display.purpose: The live score — the single most-glanced-at number on the page; tabular-nums so digits don't jitter.

title.purpose: The live clock; tabular-nums so digits don't jitter.

label.purpose: Field labels, subtitle, sport name, status text.

motion.name: tap-feedback
motion.purpose: Pill buttons invert to Signal Lavender the instant they're tapped — no transition delay, since confirmation speed matters more than polish here.

breakpoints.name: single-column
breakpoints.purpose: main is capped at max-width 480px and centered; the layout doesn't otherwise branch by breakpoint.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Full-width primary action (Join). Signal Lavender fill, dark ink text.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { width: 100%; padding: 14px; font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 600; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; border: none; border-radius: 10px; background: #b39ddb; color: #1a1a1a; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.6; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #b39ddb; outline-offset: 2px; } @media (hover: hover) { .ds-btn-primary:not(:disabled):hover { filter: brightness(1.1); } }

components.name: Score Pill (default)
components.description: Score increment/decrement control. Inverts to Signal Lavender on tap as its only feedback state.
components.css: .ds-pill-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; min-width: 64px; min-height: 56px; padding: 14px 20px; border-radius: 999px; border: 1px solid var(--border, #3a3f4a); background: var(--pill-bg, #262a33); color: #f2f2f2; font-size: 1.15rem; font-weight: 600; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; } .ds-pill-btn:active { background: #b39ddb; color: #1a1a1a; } .ds-pill-btn:disabled { opacity: 0.4; } .ds-pill-btn:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #b39ddb; outline-offset: 2px; } @media (hover: hover) { .ds-pill-btn:not(:disabled):hover { border-color: #b39ddb; } }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Pairing-code field. Card Surface background, subtle border, no icon.
components.css: .ds-input { width: 100%; padding: 14px; font-size: 1rem; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; border-radius: 10px; border: 1px solid #3a3f4a; background: #1c1f26; color: #f2f2f2; } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #b39ddb; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Team Card
components.description: Team name, live score, and its increment/decrement row.
components.css: .ds-card { background: #1c1f26; border-radius: 12px; padding: 16px; text-align: center; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; } .ds-card-title { font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 700; margin: 0 0 8px; color: #f2f2f2; overflow-wrap: anywhere; } .ds-card-score { font-size: 2.5rem; font-weight: 700; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: #f2f2f2; margin-bottom: 12px; }

components.name: Status Dot
components.description: Connection state — always pairs a colored bullet with a text label, never color alone.
components.css: .ds-dot { font-size: 0.85rem; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; } .ds-dot-connected { color: #66bb6a; } .ds-dot-pending { color: #ffb74d; }

narrative.overview: This is a control surface, not a page or an app in the marketing sense. Whether it's the operator glancing at a phone mounted courtside while also framing the camera shot, or a remote scorer half-attention on a live match at a laptop, the job is the same: glance, register a number, tap, and move on. The dark-void background and flat card layering exist so the screen doesn't glare, and so the two things that actually matter — the score and the clock — are the highest-contrast elements on it by construction, not by accident. One brand, two platforms: the web mirror expresses it in CSS custom properties; the Android app expresses the identical hex values through a Material3 ColorScheme (com.scorecast.app.theme.ScoreCastTheme). It explicitly rejects dashboard styling: no card grids beyond what a screen's actual content needs, no gradients, no hero-metric treatment, no unnecessary navigation chrome. Every element on screen is either the current game state or a control to change it. Nothing is here to look designed; it's here to be trusted at a glance during a live broadcast.
keyCharacteristics: Two-tone flat layering (void background, one card/surface tone) — no shadows anywhere, on either platform
One accent color, used only for the primary action and the "this is now selected" state
System font stack on both platforms — different literal fonts (web system-ui stack vs. Android's default Roboto), same principle
Full light/dark parity via prefers-color-scheme (web) / isSystemInDarkTheme() (Android), not a manual toggle

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Signal Lavender appears in exactly two places: the primary Join action, and confirming which pill was just tapped. It never appears as decoration, and it never carries status meaning.

rules.name: The Per-Theme Contrast Rule
rules.body: Dark mode and light mode are not palette-swaps of the same five hues; each semantic color (accent, ok, pending, danger, muted) is independently verified at >=4.5:1 against its own theme's background. Amber in particular needs to go notably darker on a light surface than intuition suggests, since amber's native luminance is high.

rules.name: The Accent-Ink Rule
rules.body: Signal Lavender is used as a fill (Join button, active pill), so its paired ink color (--accent-ink) flips with it: dark ink on the light lavender fill in dark mode, white ink on the deeper purple fill in light mode. Any new component that fills with --accent must pair it with --accent-ink, never a hardcoded ink color.

rules.name: The One Brand, Two Renderers Rule
rules.body: A color value lives conceptually in one place (DESIGN.md's Colors section) and physically in two: the CSS custom property in web-mirror/style.css and the Kotlin Color(...) constant in Theme.kt. Changing one without the other is drift, not a platform-specific decision.

rules.name: The Tabular Clock Rule
rules.body: Any element showing a live-updating number that must not visually jitter gets font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums, applied to both the clock and the score.

rules.name: The Flat-Only Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow anywhere in this system (web). Android carries a known minor divergence: Material3's default Card applies its own subtle elevation, not yet overridden to zero.

rules.name: The Hover-Gate Rule
rules.body: Every interactive element gets a :hover state, but always gated behind @media (hover: hover) so touch devices never get a stuck hover. The confirmed primary user is seated at a laptop/desk (mouse-first), so hover feedback is not optional polish here. Web-only — Android is touch-first and has no hover concept.

dos: Do keep every status indicator paired with a text label alongside its color, exactly as the connection dot already does.
Do use Signal Lavender only for the primary action and the "just tapped" confirmation state.
Do give every tappable control immediate, visible feedback.
Do keep the system font stack.
Do apply tabular-nums to any new live-updating numeric display.
Do verify every semantic color independently against both the dark and light background before shipping it.
Do pair any --accent fill with --accent-ink, never a hardcoded ink color.
Do give every interactive element a :hover state gated behind @media (hover: hover), and a visible Signal Lavender :focus-visible ring.
Do reference MaterialTheme.colorScheme.* or ScoreCastColors.* for any Android brand/status color, never a bare Color(0x...) literal.
Do update both web-mirror/style.css and Theme.kt together when a brand color changes.
donts: Don't add card-grid dashboard scaffolding, gradients, hero-metric layouts, or navigation chrome.
Don't rely on color alone to convey state.
Don't rebuild a DOM element in direct response to its own click on the same event tick.
Don't introduce a second accent color.
Don't assume a dark-mode color value works unchanged in light mode — verify contrast per theme, not once.
Don't conflate the Android LIVE/Recording tally-light red with the brand's status-danger red — different colors for a deliberately different reason (broadcast convention vs. error state).

Don't touch ScoreboardOverlay.kt's team-color strips or white score/name text as part of brand harmonization — those are driven by user-picked colors and video-legibility requirements, not app chrome.
